papers.title: On variability in local field potentials.
papers.summary: This study analyzed variability in EEG and local field potentials (LFP), showing that across-trial variance and intra-trial variance (signal power) are nearly identical outside event-related potentials. They introduced CV(power), a mean-normalized variability metric, and found LFP gamma-band power increases after stimulus onset, unlike EEG.

papers.title: Tilia Tomentosa promotes sleep, preserving sleep structure.
papers.summary: In freely moving mice, chronic treatment with Tilia tomentosa extract increased NREM sleep during the active period, reduced wakefulness, and decreased brief awakenings during resting hours without altering overall sleep structure or EEG spectral features. These findings support Tilia's sleep-promoting and sleep-stabilizing effects.

papers.title: Topographic mapping and overnight dynamics of cyclic alternating pattern subtypes in typically developing children.
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG in children, this study characterized scalp topography and overnight dynamics of cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) subtypes. Slow-frequency CAP components (A1, A2-low) declined over the night, while fast components (A2-high, A3) increased and showed frontal predominance.

papers.title: A Dry-Contact Ear-EEG System With Continuous Electrode-Skin Impedance Mismatch Monitoring for Motion Artifact Cancellation Using DRL Stimulus
papers.summary: This paper presents a dry-contact ear-EEG system with continuous electrode-skin impedance mismatch monitoring via a DRL stimulus. The system achieved motion artifact power reductions of 6.5-12.6 dB while preserving alpha-band modulation, demonstrating feasibility for wearable EEG.

papers.title: Human Recorded Signal Properties of Endovascular EEG Compared to Conventional Scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This study evaluated endovascular EEG (eEEG) signals in five humans during Wada tests, finding about 3.7 times higher power than scalp EEG and higher coupling to scalp EEG, supporting its potential for neuromonitoring and brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: No evidence for modulation of the readiness potential by respiratory phase during natural breathing.
papers.summary: Reanalysing EEG data, this study found no evidence for modulation of the readiness potential by respiratory phase after controlling for movement onset confound. Bayesian analyses supported absence of coupling, highlighting pitfalls in phase-amplitude analyses.

papers.title: Clinically altered brain activity may not look like aged brain activity: Implications for brain-age modeling and biomarker strategies.
papers.summary: The study examined brain-age gap (BAG) estimation from EEG spectral power in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), finding that models trained on healthy controls systematically underpredict age in clinical populations due to divergent age-related EEG trends, questioning the interpretability of EEG-BAG as a biomarker for individual aging.

papers.title: Harmonizing complexity and efficiency: Helix Fusion HarmonyNet's breakthrough in EEG-based postoperative delirium recognition.
papers.summary: The paper presents Helix Fusion HarmonyNet (HFHN), a lightweight and interpretable deep learning framework for EEG-based postoperative delirium detection, achieving 100% accuracy in Fourier-domain and maintaining high accuracy with sparse electrodes while reducing computational cost significantly.

papers.title: Multilevel brain functional heterogeneity in major depressive disorder based on normative modeling of multicenter resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: Using normative modeling on multicenter resting-state EEG data, the study found that EEG abnormalities in major depressive disorder (MDD) are highly individualized, with significant deviations mainly in prefrontal regions and orbitofrontal cortex, particularly in beta-band relative power, and limbic network involvement.

papers.title: Multi-branch heterogeneous network of exploiting complementary multi-view features for decoding finger motor imagery EEG.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-branch heterogeneous network (MBHN) with channel adaptive kernels to decode finger motor imagery from EEG, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy of 58.49% by exploiting complementary multi-view features.

papers.title: In-home validation of wrist actigraphy against portable electroencephalography for sleep assessment in older adults.
papers.summary: In 49 community-dwelling older adults over 217 nights, wrist actigraphy versus portable EEG showed acceptable accuracy for average total sleep time (ICC=0.73, MAPE=11%) but poor accuracy for sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset (MAPE>50%). Actigraphy is suitable for estimating average sleep duration but not for sleep fragmentation indices in this population.

papers.title: Muscle age acceleration shapes resting-state brain connectivity: an EEG study on older adults.
papers.summary: This study examined resting-state EEG connectivity in older adults stratified by muscle age acceleration, finding that decelerated muscle age is associated with lower connectivity in alpha and beta bands, suggesting muscle aging trajectories influence brain network organization.

papers.title: EEG Oscillations in Guided Mindfulness versus Mind-Wandering in Young Adults: Effects of Auditory Task Instruction and Naturalistic Video
papers.summary: This study used EEG to compare alpha and theta oscillations during mindfulness versus mind-wandering in 20 non-expert meditators, finding that mindfulness significantly increased posterior alpha power, while theta was larger when auditory instructions were present. The results suggest that acute mindfulness effects are most consistently observed as increases in posterior alpha-band activity.

papers.title: Is Ultra-Long-Term Subscalp EEG Ready to Go "Solo"? Transforming the Landscape of Antiseizure Medication Management.
papers.summary: This editorial commentary discusses the potential of ultra-long-term subscalp EEG to transform antiseizure medication management, despite the abstract being empty. It likely argues for the clinical utility of this technology.

papers.title: Dry-electrode EEG tracks alpha changes during accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This letter reports on using dry-electrode EEG to track alpha changes during accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) in treatment-resistant depression, suggesting that dry-electrode EEG can capture relevant neural changes. The abstract is empty.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of the Flow Experience: An EEG Microstate Analysis.
papers.summary: This study used EEG microstate analysis in 43 participants during a video game to examine flow states, finding that flow was associated with reduced duration and frequency of microstates C and E, which are linked to default mode network activity. This supports the idea that flow involves diminished self-referential processing.

papers.title: Breathable, Biocompatible, Ultrathin Bilayer Epidermal Electrodes for Long-Term and Motion-Artifact-Resistant Monitoring ofHigh-Fidelity Electrophysiological Signals.
papers.summary: This study introduces a breathable, biocompatible, ultrathin bilayer epidermal electrode for long-term, motion-artifact-resistant electrophysiological monitoring, demonstrating high-fidelity acquisition of EMG, EOG, EEG, and ECG signals. The electrode achieves reliable muscle fatigue assessment and gesture recognition, offering a strategy for stable low-impedance interfaces.

papers.title: Modified shuffle Net-DCNN architecture with cepstral and spectral feature for epileptic seizure detection using EEG signal.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.summary: The study introduces a hybrid model combining Modified Shuffle Net V2 and Deep Convolutional Neural Network for epileptic seizure detection from EEG signals. The model achieved approximately 94% accuracy with 90% training data.

papers.title: A dual-branch time-frequency fusion network for EEG-based classification of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a dual-branch time-frequency fusion network (DBTF-Net) for EEG-based classification of Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and cognitively normal subjects. The model achieved 86.36% accuracy for three-class classification and up to 92.13% for binary tasks.

papers.title: Implant-Grade Neural Sensing with Artifact-Resilient Computational Intelligence Preserves Spatial Fidelity of HFO Biomarkers in Epilepsy.
papers.summary: The paper evaluates a wireless implantable neural interface for preserving high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) in epilepsy monitoring. The system retained ~82% of clinical HFOs and localized the seizure onset zone with 84% sensitivity and 90% specificity.

papers.title: A novel approach to dyslexia detection: combining EEG data and cognitive tasks with advanced machine learning.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: The study combines EEG data and cognitive screening tasks with machine learning for dyslexia detection in children. The Random Forest classifier achieved 98.69% accuracy when fusing both modalities, and dyslexic individuals showed elevated delta/theta energy.

papers.title: Targeting Nav1.6: a promising strategy against cognitive impairment in maternal separation-sensitive mice.
papers.journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
papers.summary: The study investigates the role of Nav1.6 in cognitive impairment induced by maternal separation in mice. Hippocampal Nav1.6 knockdown alleviated cognitive deficits, reduced neuroinflammation, and altered autophagy markers.

papers.title: Meditation styles are highly discriminable from EEG at the subject level with limited generalization across the population: a machine-learning study.
papers.summary: This study assessed whether EEG-based machine learning can classify three meditation styles (Shamatha, Vipassana, Metta) and mind-wandering in experienced meditators. It found high intra-subject accuracy but much lower inter-subject generalization, indicating subject-specific neural signatures and challenges for subject-independent classification.

papers.title: Machine learning classification of mild Alzheimer's disease using EEG during emotional processing.
papers.summary: The study used EEG recorded during emotional movie clips and machine learning classifiers to discriminate mild Alzheimer's disease patients from healthy controls, achieving best performance with LASSO for positive/neutral stimuli in parietal and posterior gamma bands and CatBoost for high-arousal negative emotions in frontal gamma/theta bands. These results suggest EEG during emotional processing may provide biomarkers for mild AD.

papers.title: Altered integration of bodily and visual signals in visual snow syndrome.
papers.journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
papers.summary: In a case-control EEG study of 18 visual snow syndrome (VSS) patients and 16 matched controls, VSS participants showed altered heartbeat-evoked potentials and reduced condition-dependent differentiation, with the relationship between interoceptive and exteroceptive markers moderated by group and associated with symptom intensity. Source localization implicated a left frontotemporal network. This suggests VSS involves altered interoceptive-exteroceptive integration during visual perception.

papers.title: Material and Design Strategies of Soft Microelectrode Arrays for Implantable Cardiac Interfaces.
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in soft implantable cardiac microelectrode arrays (MEAs), covering fundamental cardiac electrophysiology, material candidates, state-of-the-art MEAs for electrophysiological mapping and electrotherapy, as well as transparent, bioresorbable, and multimodal devices integrating electrical, optical, and mechanical functions. It highlights future directions for next-generation cardiovascular diagnosis and therapy.

papers.title: Characteristics of sustained attention impairment in individuals under simulated positive acceleration stress: separation effect of early and late stage cognitive processing.
papers.summary: This study investigated sustained attention impairment under simulated positive acceleration stress using lower body negative pressure and EEG. Results showed a dissociation between early and late processing stages, with reduced P2 latency (enhanced early perceptual processing) and reduced P300 amplitude (impaired late response selection), suggesting adaptive compensation.

papers.title: Electrophysiological markers of surprise-induced failures of visual and auditory awareness.
papers.summary: Using EEG in 33 participants performing surprise-induced blindness and deafness paradigms, the study identified a late parietal positivity akin to the novelty P3 that habituated alongside behavioral deficits, suggesting shared mechanisms for both phenomena. Individual deficits were not correlated across modalities, and surprise in one modality did not affect the other, indicating modality-specific attentional limitations.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Evidence of Enhanced Cognitive Control Following Auditory Control Enhancement (ACE) Therapy: A Pilot RCT in Schizophrenia-Spectrum Disorders with Persistent Auditory Hallucinations.
papers.summary: In a pilot single-blind randomized controlled trial, individuals with schizophrenia who received Auditory Control Enhancement (ACE) therapy (active tDCS paired with Auditory Cognitive Control Training) showed increased attention modulation (larger ASSR attend-ignore difference), greater beta desynchronization during proactive inhibition, and reduced physical aspects of auditory hallucinations compared to sham. No such changes were observed in the sham group.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Changes in Brain Activity Among Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated With Conventional Complete Dentures and Tooth-Supported Overdentures Using Electroencephalography: An In Vivo Study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study compared EEG-based brain activity in 36 edentulous patients rehabilitated with conventional complete dentures, tooth-supported overdentures without attachments, and with stud attachments. After two months, all three groups showed significant increases in EEG-derived cortical activity, with no significant between-group differences, indicating that restoration of masticatory function is associated with enhanced cortical electrical activity regardless of prosthesis type.

papers.title: Targeted stimulation of face-selective visual cortex at retrieval boosts associative face memory in healthy young adults.
papers.summary: This study tested whether targeted intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) of the right occipital face area before retrieval could selectively enhance associative memory for faces versus scenes in healthy young adults. They found that pre-retrieval iTBS selectively improved face associative memory but not scene memory, supporting the encoding-pattern reinstatement framework, although EEG multivariate pattern analysis was inconclusive on the mechanism.

papers.title: Patterns and Clinical Predictors of Antiseizure Medication Use in Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: This multi-center retrospective cohort study of 467 pediatric TBI patients identified clinical predictors of antiseizure medication (ASM) prescription during hospitalization and at discharge. Intracranial injury on imaging, moderate Glasgow Coma Scale score, admission to neurology/neurosurgery, and immediate seizures were associated with inpatient ASM use; neuroimaging abnormalities and immediate seizures predicted discharge ASM prescription.

papers.title: Comparative study of chlorophyll measurement in Physcomitrium patens moss using a conventional microscope adapted for combined 2D+1D imaging and spectral analysis
papers.summary: This preprint describes a simple method for attaching a miniature fiber spectrometer to a conventional microscope to enable combined 2D imaging and 1D spectral analysis. The authors demonstrated the setup's performance for quantitative chlorophyll measurement in Physcomitrium patens moss, comparing color imaging and spectral sampling approaches.

papers.title: [Gq-GPCR upregulation in reactive astrocytes: implication for neurological disorders].
papers.journal: Nihon yakurigaku zasshi. Folia pharmacologica Japonica
papers.summary: This review discusses the upregulation of Gq-GPCR P2Y1 receptor in reactive astrocytes across brain disorders and its role in promoting neuronal hyperexcitability. Using astrocyte-specific overexpression in mice, the authors identified the P2Y1R-IGFBP2 signaling axis as a common pathological feature, with IGFBP2 enhancing glutamatergic transmission and contributing to seizure susceptibility.

papers.title: The Efficacy of Therapies for Phantom Limb Pain in Amputees Assessed via Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Electroencephalography (EEG) Measures of Cortical Reorganization: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review assessed nonpharmacologic therapies for phantom limb pain using fMRI and EEG measures of cortical reorganization. Most effective therapies were associated with changes in sensorimotor cortex organization, but the relationship between cortical changes and pain reduction was inconsistent, suggesting a multifactorial network-level condition.

papers.title: Status Epilepticus and Lateralized Periodic Discharges (LPDs) in Cannabis Withdrawal Syndrome: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 53-year-old woman who developed tonic-clonic status epilepticus and lateralized periodic discharges after abrupt cannabis withdrawal. Treatment with anticonvulsants led to clinical improvement and resolution of EEG abnormalities, highlighting the need for anticonvulsant treatment in such cases.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Mobile-Delivered Exercise and Yoga Programs on Depressive Symptom Reduction in Employees: Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial compared 12-session mobile-delivered adaptive exercise and yoga programs against a cognitive behavioral therapy-based self-care control for reducing depressive symptoms and stress in 75 employees. The yoga group showed significantly greater improvement in depressive symptoms at 4-week follow-up compared to control and exhibited sustained improvement in cognitive stress responses, while exercise showed more modest, less sustained effects.

papers.title: Preparation of Plasma Membrane Vesicles, Lysosomes, Proteoliposomes and Alternative Sample Types for SSM-Based Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This chapter provides a detailed protocol for preparing plasma membrane vesicles and lysosomes from mammalian cell culture for SSM-based electrophysiology, using nitrogen decompression and sucrose gradient centrifugation. It also covers alternative sample types and preparation strategies, including proteoliposomes, and reports enrichment of 14 marker proteins to evaluate purity.

papers.title: Machine learning-enabled chemical ecology for integrated pest management: from volatiles to field applications.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how machine learning is applied across the semiochemical discovery and implementation pipeline for integrated pest management, from volatile detection to field deployment. It proposes a 4-stage framework (detection, design, deployment, decision support) and highlights challenges, including data scarcity and limited field validation, with recommendations for developing reusable datasets.

papers.title: Safety and Feasibility of Deep Sedation With a Tulip Airway and Jaw Elevation Device During Electrophysiology Procedures: A Single-Center Experience of 647 Consecutive Cases.
papers.summary: This single-center retrospective study evaluated the safety and feasibility of deep sedation with a Tulip airway and jaw elevation device in 647 patients undergoing electrophysiology procedures. All procedures were completed without sedation discontinuation, with one intubation (0.2%) and three procedure-related complications (0.5%), indicating safety in selected lower-risk patients.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
